attempts.summary: Established an IKEv2/IPsec site-to-site tunnel between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) over the transit network (10.10.0.0/30), carrying lan-a (10.10.1.0/24, behind node1, host node3) and lan-b (10.10.2.0/24, behind node2, host node4). Mapped physical interface adjacency via ARP probing since all nodes shared one platform-assigned management subnet with unaddressed secondary interfaces. Configured static addressing on all routed interfaces, static cross-LAN routes on node3/node4, VyOS site-to-site IPsec (AES256-SHA256, PSK), and OPNsense's Swanctl model plus a custom pf pass rule on enc0 (had to work around two OPNsense quirks: LegacyLinkField for ipsec.enable is read-only via the model API and must be set directly in $config, and filter rules using interface=ipsec are silently dropped, requiring the literal enc0 device name with explicit direction=in). Verified bidirectional ping between node3 and node4 using their private addresses, and confirmed via tcpdump that only ESP crosses the transit wire while plaintext ICMP is visible only on each LAN segment. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for all four nodes: captured pre-restart boot identity and IPsec/connectivity health, triggered each node's native reboot, polled until exec access returned, proved boot identity changed, and reverified addressing, IPsec re-establishment, and encrypted node3↔node4 connectivity after every restart.
